lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I heard, Chiron, that as a god you wanted to die.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: You heard right, Menippus. And here I am, dead—though I could have lived forever.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: What made you fall for death? It's not exactly popular with most people.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: I'll explain, since you're no idiot. Immortality had stopped being enjoyable.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You didn't enjoy seeing the light while you were alive?

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: No, Menippus. Pleasure needs variety; it's not a simple thing. Living forever, always enjoying the same things—the sun, the light, food, the same seasons turning, everything happening in the same order, one after another—I got tired of it. The fun wasn't in the endless repetition; it was in not having everything the same all the time.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Fair enough. So how do you like it down here, since you chose it yourself?

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: Not bad at all. Equality's very democratic, and it doesn't make much difference if you're in the light or the dark. Besides, no thirst or hunger like up there—we're free of all that.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Watch yourself, Chiron. Don't let your own argument trip you up.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: If the same old things got boring in life, won't the same happen here? Everything's the same again, so you'll want a change and try to move on to another life. Which I don't think is possible.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: So what should one do, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: What they say a sensible person does: be content with what's in front of you, and don't find any of it unbearable.
